item.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
item.description: In October, 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Halloween temperatures have been trending hotter. Here's what the data shows
item.description: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.
item.content:encoded: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.

item.title: Arizona's lifeline to the Colorado River is drying up. Its designers warned us decades ago
item.description: Arizona has now joined a lawsuit against the Trump administration's plan for sharing the Colorado River. But history shows water planners there saw big cuts to their water supply coming.

item.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

item.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
item.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
